about: MUTATING — moves the forge's Forgejo data off the root filesystem onto the boss-data drive and keeps its path: /opt/forgejo/data becomes a bind mount of <boss-data mount>/forgejo-data by an fstab line beneath the drive's by-UUID line, so the compose file and every script that reads /opt/forgejo/data are unchanged (infra/forge/move-forgejo-data.sh; backlog 016aeea3, car 2 of b2d5b546, from design ebe9e48e as David decided it — the 92G package registry drove the urgent disk alarm c4da71b0). In design 17835005's shape and authorised per run by David's passkey: it declares requires_approval with plan-a-forgejo-data-move as its plan_verb, so the runner renders the plan onto the request's approve step, runs this only after a passkey on the approvers list signs those bytes, and hands the script sha256 of the SIGNED plan; the script re-renders the plan with the command --plan uses and changes nothing unless the bytes hash alike. It takes no path: what moves and where is read from the host, never a param. The write reads the proof's before half (Forgejo's /api/healthz, refs/heads/main inside the container, the container's /data being /opt/forgejo/data by device and inode, the manifest of the converge's stamp through the registry) — a failure there is still a refusal, so a leg that cannot be read is found before anything moves — then holds the converge (unless a hold stands), stops Forgejo with docker compose stop -t 60 and records its running state, StartedAt and RestartCount (the plan names the container's restart policy, under which dockerd may start it again on its own), reads main with host git off the disk, re-checks no other running container mounts the source and no host process holds anything under it, measures it and holds it to the approved ceiling and the target's free space, copies with rsync -aHAXS --numeric-ids --delete, verifies with an rsync -aHAXSc --dry-run --itemize-changes pass that must list nothing, compares both sides' per-entry counts, and builds the new fstab in a temporary file checked with findmnt --verify --tab-file. Before the rename a failure starts Forgejo again on the untouched source and releases the hold, exit 1; so does a container found no longer as the stop left it. Then it marks the target as served (a later move onto a served target is refused, since a rollback leaves Forgejo's writes there; the marker records the stamp and manifest sha the rollback proves, and a failure before the rename removes it), renames the source to /opt/forgejo/data.pre-move-<first 8 hex of the drive's UUID>, makes the empty mountpoint immutable (so an unmounted bind is a Forgejo that cannot start, never an empty one), moves the verified fstab into place, daemon-reloads, mounts THAT path (never mount -a) and confirms the target's UUID at /forgejo-data, re-checks the container is still as the stop left it (a Forgejo started behind its back is stopped, exit 1), starts it — a real start, StartedAt must move — and proves healthz, main equal to the disk's, the container's /data being the moved copy by device and inode, and the same manifest, then releases its own hold. After the rename nothing is undone by guess: the state is printed, the hold stays, a failed proof stops Forgejo again, exit 1, and the rollback is its own approval verb (roll-back-forgejo-data-move), as is the restart of a stopped Forgejo (restart-forgejo). The old copy stays on / until delete-forgejo-premove-copy, its own approval verb, deletes it — no sooner than 24 hours after the move went live. The forge's git, CI, registry pulls and every gate and train stall for the window. Own timeout: a copy and a checksum pass over ~100 GB.
